text_to_speech: For me, being a researcher means always facing questions and trying to solve and deal with problems. On the other hand, it also means failing many times and then getting back up, continuing to study rebuilding the idea and looking for new angles that we hadn't thought of yet. IBM focuses on things that are very interesting and innovative. Subjects that represent the hottest topics and most competitive areas in academia. I knew I wanted to do research but in industry because industry addresses very diverse issues such as teamwork, which is very significant. And right here at IBM I have that combination. It's still research that is academically interesting but you also benefit from the collaborations and working with people. Using homomorphic encryption and what we're seeking to create the tools we're building with machine learning We want to allow large organizations such as hospitals to upload their information to the cloud while encrypted maintaining their patients' data privacy while allowing someone remotely to access and train on that data without being familiar with the information and still give the customer good results and what they need. The IT world today does not yet have enough representation for women. I'd like to see much more. It's a very interesting world And there's no reason more women aren't in it. You can also have much more fruitful discussions when there's a different mindset and it will also bolster diversity. This is my chance to call on all women: Come on in! We're having fun here.

youtube_description:
Moran Baruch, machine learning and cybersecurity researcher at IBM Research – Haifa, explains how her team uses homomorphic encryption and machine learning to provide better security for cloud-based data so it can be analyzed without being exposed. Moran loves being part of a team that invents new technology, and hopes to see more women join her in the IT field.

Visit the IBM Research - Haifa lab's website to learn more: https://research.ibm.com/labs/haifa/index.html
